subject: Hypershift on‑prem cutover — intermittent egress failures and connection starvation
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-04-10T09:05:12-07:00
Subject: Hypershift on-prem cutover — intermittent egress failures and connection starvation

Team — opening an escalation for a customer that's mid cutover to Hypershift (private on‑prem stack). Symptoms started at 05:30 PT and persist intermittently: outbound TCP flows to object storage (S3 endpoints) stall with long SYN retries, then later succeed; other flows time out. Key observations from initial triage attached.

What we see in conn-trace.log / pcap sample: repeated SYN retries from application hosts, a flurry of SYN, SYN-ACK (server), retransmit SYN; occasional RSTs from a transit device. Traces indicate:
- bursts of asymmetric path (egress from host -> edge -> partner, return takes different route via transit GW)
- NAT ephemeral port reuse (multiple hosts get same source port after cutover)
- MTU fragmentation signs: PMTU discovery ICMP 'fragmentation needed' seen in some traces
- hairpinning between private subnets (traffic to S3 proxy looped through NAT appliance)

We've got a support contact at Brighthost (cc'd in infra-team) — they agreed to look at SNAT port pools but asked for more concrete evidence. Attaching topology diagram and sample captures.

Immediate ask: can network (Marissa) and infra (Vanessa) confirm number of SNAT ports available on the transit appliance, current conntrack totals, and whether any security group/stateful rules could be clearing ESTABLISHED flows? Also need approval for a temporary MSS clamp and a short canary reroute to a dedicated NAT gateway if it helps.

I'll run a short tcpdump + conntrack snapshot and push logs to the ticket.

Diego
Engineering — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: conn-trace.log (text), pcap-sample.pcap (pcap), topology-diagram.png (image)

Subject: Re: Hypershift on-prem cutover — intermittent egress failures and connection starvation

Thanks Diego — I pulled the attachments. Quick checklist from netops:
- Need a 1-minute tcpdump during a failure window (capture filter: host s3.amazonaws.com or host obj.brighthost.net)
- Export /proc/net/nf_conntrack counts (before, during, after)
- Show iptables nat POSTROUTING SNAT table and current source port range on the transit appliance
- If possible, run `ss -tn state established` on affected app hosts and include counts by src_port range

My working hypothesis: SNAT port exhaustion+asymmetric return causing server replies to be routed back through a different NAT instance that doesn't have the conntrack entry -> RSTs. Also want to confirm PMTU path — if PMTU fails and we get fragments dropped by middlebox, TCP stalls and retransmits.

If you can confirm conntrack spike and SNAT slot reuse, I'll open an emergency change to expand SNAT pool and add a temporary hairpin bypass for the cutover. We should also test a temporary kernel-level MSS clamp (1300) on a canary host — that typically resolves fragmentation-related stalls fast.

Marissa
Network Reliability Lead

Date: 2028-04-10T10:02:14-07:00
Subject: Re: Hypershift on-prem cutover — intermittent egress failures and connection starvation

Hi Diego / Marissa — we pulled the pcap. Two quick notes from Brighthost edge:
1) We're seeing source port collisions across hosts that line up with conntrack timeouts on our SNAT boxes. When a new host reuses a port that a previous flow still needs, replies are being misdelivered or dropped.
2) We observe PMTU ICMP 'frag needed' messages from a few hops but the appliance is configured to drop ICMP for the control-plane. That blocks PMTU and leads to retransmit storms when MSS isn't clamped.

Immediate recommendations: increase SNAT ephemeral range and conntrack timeout temporarily (we can push a config change on our side). Also allow ICMP 'fragmentation needed' to pass for the cutover window or enable MSS clamp on the transit appliance.

I created ticket BR-98213 and will monitor while you run experiments. If you want, we can also provision a dedicated NAT gateway for the cutover for the next 4 hours and route canary traffic there — low risk and quick rollback.

Alex Morris
Platform Ops — Brighthost
https://support.brighthost.com/ticket/BR-98213

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Morris <alex@brighthost.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-04-10T10:35:09-07:00
Subject: Re: Hypershift on-prem cutover — intermittent egress failures and connection starvation

Update — ran two quick experiments on a canary host (host-c-03):
- Applied iptables mangle rule to clamp MSS to 1300 on SYN packets (iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1300).
- Captured 120s tcpdump while inducing load to object store.

Results: fragmentation-related retransmits dropped by ~60%, successful connections up from ~55% to ~82% during the window. However, SYN_RECV counts on the transit appliance remained elevated and we still saw a handful of flows being reset mid-session. conn-trace.log attached.

Given Alex's note on SNAT pool reuse, I'm comfortable requesting the temporary dedicated NAT gateway — we can route a small percentage (10%) of cutover traffic there as a canary and increase if stable. That avoids pushing config changes across all edge appliances.

Requesting approval for:
- Temporary NAT gateway provisioning (Brighthost) and routing 10% canary for 2 hours, then evaluate;
- If canary looks good, expand to 50% while we increase SNAT ephemeral range and conntrack timeouts;
- Temporary allowlist for ICMP "fragmentation needed" for the cutover window only.

Change request: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-4572

Diego

Thanks for the clear diagnostics and runbook Diego and Alex. Approve the canary NAT gateway approach. Please follow this rollout plan:

1) Provision dedicated NAT gateway (Brighthost) and verify no config drift in firewall rules.
2) Route 10% canary traffic from the cutover cohort for 30 minutes. Monitor: SYN retries, conntrack usage, and application success rate.
3) If metrics stable, ramp to 50% for 45 minutes. Maintain tcpdump on the canary host and scrape metrics to the incident dashboard.
4) If at any point the canary shows increased RSTs or new failure classes, rollback to 0% and revert to MSS clamp on canaries.

Security note: allowlist for ICMP frag-needed must be scoped to the two egress paths and limited to the change window. I'll loop in Security for a rapid exception. Also ensure we capture a post-mortem with specific tunables (conntrack limits, SNAT range, MSS clamp) so we can bake the fix into the cutover runbook.

Vanessa Ortiz
